# Maintenance history carried into the stack workflow

Nate approved the visual design on October 21, 2026, and requested Jeremiah's historical process before implementation. Reviewed local history against GitHub main `d92276995f2f7b34dedbc7a8dfa8a4fa2ea4d013`, current labels through `gh label list`, original PR bodies, and current workflow scripts.

## Preserve

- **Contract before fix.** Jeremiah added the explicit contract gate in [#4214](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4214): reproducible behavior is not necessarily a defect. Preserve that gate, while applying current skills' requirement to inspect docs, protocol, history and maintainer decisions before escalating. Do not resurrect the older habit of asking the maintainer whenever code alone is ambiguous.
- **Closed contributions remain evidence.** [#4780](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4780) requires reading associated closed external PRs, including comments and timeline. Gate closure does not mean a rejected implementation. Preserve useful code and attribution; avoid competing replacement PRs by default.
- **Explicit supersession remains authoritative.** Nate [closed #5656 in favor of #5779](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5656#issuecomment-6296713451), preserving the earlier contribution and credit. Its earlier dependency on #5671 does not authorize reviving that pair to manufacture a stack. Distinguish an administrative gate closure from a maintainer's recorded selection among overlapping proposals.
- **Human intervention persists.** [#2981](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/2981) repaired repeated duplicate closures. Current duplicate automation uses `potential-duplicate`, a three-day cooldown, any subsequent human comment, negative/confused reactions, and prior auto-closure evidence. These can stop closure; the temporary label is consumed. Do not recalculate a rejected duplicate verdict on every scan. Record adjudication and evidence revision.
- **Missing reproduction is a separate lifecycle.** `needs MRE` drives a seven-day author-inactivity closer; maintainer-authored issues are exempt. `needs more info` does not invoke the same timer. Current bot retains comments and edit evidence; label presence alone is not permission to close. The new trial produces recommendations and leaves existing closers responsible for their own actions.
- **Gate ownership matters.** [#4518](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4518) documents a label replacement race that erased `missing-issue-link` and broke reopening. Preserve labels from other owners. `missing-issue-link`, `bypass-issue-check`, `trusted-contributor`, and `prs welcome` are protected by the current triage helper. Do not infer distrust from a gate label or remove it as cleanup.
- **Community participation has explicit routes.** [#4557](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4557) introduced issue-level `prs welcome` to waive assignment, not the issue-link requirement. It deliberately replaced misleading `good first issue` expectations. Assignment can reopen a gated PR; manual reopen/removal of the gate label grants sticky bypass. Current [#5048](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5048) keeps linked PRs open while awaiting assignment, superseding the older close-all behavior.
- **Label precision and ownership.** [#4654](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4654) explicitly removed guessed labels and label suggestions from PR prose. Marvin owns category/area classification; the stack controller consumes actual labels and records internal bins in artifacts. Release categories depend on exact names, including `breaking change`, `bug`, `enhancement`, and `security`. Live `breaking` is not equivalent to `breaking change`; do not silently normalize or mutate it.
- **Intentional automation triggers.** [#3124](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/3124) constrained automatic issue triage and guarded the human-applied `triage-martian` trigger. Do not apply this label from an agent or launch a second competing fixer. Snapshot ongoing activity and ownership before dispatch/publication.
- **Bounded small-model work is established precedent.** Jeremiah tried Haiku for narrow labeling/dedupe in [#1613](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/1613). This supports trying cheap models, not assuming their current quality or price. Measure accepted output and human corrections. Later model upgrades do not establish why the experiment changed without further evidence.
- **Silence is often the correct public output.** Labeling/dedupe prompts suppress unsolicited commentary, except narrowly defined messages. Keep detailed traces private and public descriptions concise. Review real bot findings on their merits, cap speculative repair loops, and preserve issue-author credit ([#5410](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5410)).
- **A green orchestration run is insufficient.** [#4555](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4555), [#4560](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4560), and [#4645](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/4645) fixed silent tool-permission/sandbox failures. Check actual evidence, test artifacts, PRs and stack membership; keep operational failures distinct from negative issue verdicts.

## Encode with gh and existing labels

Collect paginated REST issue/comment/timeline/PR/review/check/stack data using `gh api`, preserving failures rather than treating missing pages as empty. Read all-state linked PRs; bounded search is additional evidence, not proof of absence. Snapshot live labels and exact source SHAs. Use area/category labels to narrow coherent batches, with unlabelled items still eligible for classification. Treat priority labels as hints, not proof of severity or rejection.

Deterministically route existing PRs to review; human hold/draft/DO NOT MERGE signals to held review; gate labels to contribution-state handling; `needs MRE` and `potential-duplicate` to their evidence/decision lanes. Labels do not override newer comments, supported-version evidence, or the intended contract. Refresh them immediately before publication. Security goes to restricted review; an auth label alone is not a security verdict.

No new workflow-state labels, manual label changes, bypasses, assignment changes, automatic comments/closures, merges, or schedules are needed for the first trial. The controller's persistent ledger tracks claims, costs and internal decisions without overloading community-facing labels.
